newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firmer, interbank rate rises late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firmer, interbank rate rises late.

text.p: The Thai baht was slightly higher against the dollar late on Thursday as some profit-taking in the American unit helped clip the baht's earlier weakness, dealers said.
The baht was traded at 25.614-25.619 to the dollar late against 25.619-25.624 earlier, dealers said. The baht was at 25.600-25.605 late on Wednesday.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.59 against 25.58 on Wednesday, the lowest fixing in several years.
"There was selling of the dollar in late afternoon. But the market activities remained thin as most players already squared their positions," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
She added the dollar's rise abroad and year-end demand for the U.S. currency triggered some buying interest for the dollar in the morning.
The overnight interbank rate rose to 14.50 percent late from 13.75-14.00 in early morning on tighter liquidity, dealers said.
Dealers said there steady demand for funds at the year end. The Bank of Thailand's refusal to inject funds and alleviate tight market liquidity was another factor for the rate's increase, they added.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was at 9.50/10.50 satangs per dollar late from 9.50/10.25 in early morning.
